order: Fix a sharper edge left in the stable-alias fix itself. When the alias a live checkout was created through is later removed, sweep-time path re-lookup falls back to the lexical alias spelling while git's own listed path stays canonical, and that mismatch causes the sweep to remove the live canonical checkout. Capture the canonical identity exactly once, at creation time, when every path component is guaranteed to exist, and have the live-set comparison use that identity instead of a sweep-time re-lookup. Pin a regression for the alias-removal case, and confirm it fails without the fix. Diagnose and fix an intermittent review-lane test failure, since git holds a newly created worktree locked for the whole checkout while it is already visible in the list. A kill in that window leaves the worktree locked forever, and a removal command cannot clear a locked worktree, so the terminate-signal branch must wait out the registration window exactly as the kill-signal branch does.
claims: The canonical identity is captured once at creation, when every path component is guaranteed to exist, and the live-set comparison uses it rather than a sweep-time re-lookup. The alias-removal case is pinned as a regression, and the intermittent review-lane failure traced to a locked-worktree window at checkout. The terminate-signal branch now waits out the registration window as the kill-signal branch does, confirmed clean at 114 runs across five attempts. Verifier and router finish clean on this same local run, and registry follows right behind, backed by the pull request's own run.
